Unity: The Unity party sees Mars as but a piece of the larger puzzle that is humanity's settlement of the solar system. As such, they tend to have favor with factions outside of Mars, but are not well liked by the Martians themselves. Especially those that side with Mars First.
Greens: The Greens are a haughty environmentalist group that touts the terraforming effort as humankind's atonement for ruining Earth. They therefore push for focusing all available resources on it — a view that's well aligned with the UNMI committee's. As a result, the two factions have close ties together.
Scientists: A loose collective of rich entrepreneurs that view Mars as an opportunity to advance humanity's grasp of the sciences to never-before seen heights. They want to be the vanguard of this progress, and are willing to move heaven and earth to see it through.
Mars First: Mars' populist centrist party that puts emphasis on the terraforming being for the Martians first, and everyone else second. They invest heavily in building up and improving the living standards of the colonists, at the expense of projects of other parties.
Industrialists: The Industrialist party champions the notion that, in the long run, the terraforming will go smoother if the corporations are allowed to profit as much as they want at its outset, and grow stronger. Critics discard this as a ruse to profiteer at humanity's expense. But because Mars is run by corporations, the party remains popular.
Reds: The Reds are Mars' nationalist conservatives who want the planet to remain the same as when they were founded. To this end, they pursue the outlandish goal of halting the terraforming, by enticing companies to do literally anything else. A position that makes them mortal enemies of the Greens.
